# This is an INLINE packaging description (spec §5.1): the bytes come from the author's own
# release, but which asset to install and what to name the command is the index talking --
# so the client downgrades the trust level to index-toyfile.
# There is deliberately no [sha256]: inline entries follow the upstream's newest tag, so
# pinning one version's bytes would turn the next release into a checksum mismatch that reads
# like a poisoning warning. First install is still pinned by trust on first use.
name    = "dive"
desc    = "A tool for exploring each layer in a docker image"
license = "MIT"

[bin]
# The path on the right was read out of a real archive that was unpacked and inspected.
dive = "dive"

[artifact]
"darwin/amd64" = "dive_{version}_darwin_amd64.tar.gz"
"darwin/arm64" = "dive_{version}_darwin_arm64.tar.gz"
"linux/amd64" = "dive_{version}_linux_amd64.tar.gz"
"linux/arm64" = "dive_{version}_linux_arm64.tar.gz"
